paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul writes from prison and asks the believers to walk in a manner worthy of the calling they have received (Ephesians 4:1). What does that look like? "All humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love" (Ephesians 4:2). And the unity is already there, because it's the unity of the Spirit, so your job is to preserve it, not build it from scratch (Ephesians 4:3).

Why can you hold on to it? Because the things you share are bigger than anything that could split you: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all (Ephesians 4:4-6). Then Paul says grace has been given to each one of us (Ephesians 4:7). Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, and pastors and teachers to equip the saints for works of ministry (Ephesians 4:11-12). That means the church isn't a show where a few people do the work and everybody else watches, friend. You are on the team, and I'm not asking you to carry the whole bakery alone!

So what happens as the body grows up? We stop being infants tossed about by every wind of teaching, and we start speaking the truth in love (Ephesians 4:14-15). Christ Himself is the head, and the whole body grows "through the work of each individual part" (Ephesians 4:16). So the next time you wonder whether your small part matters, remember it does. Be patient with the people beside you, stay rooted in the truth, and do your part in love.
